The canvas with no edges

Boundless is where teams think out loud.

An infinite, pan-and-zoom whiteboard for diagrams, roadmaps, and live brainstorms. Drop shapes, link them with connectors that stay attached, sketch freehand, and zoom from a single sticky note out to your whole quarter — all in the browser, all yours.

Steps of undo history

What makes it feel alive

Boundless is built on a real world↔screen camera transform, an object model, and an undo stack — the kind of app you'd never assemble out of page blocks.

True infinite canvas

Scroll to zoom toward your cursor, space-drag or two-finger pan, and the dotted grid scales with you. The math keeps the point under your pointer perfectly fixed.

Connectors that stick

Draw an arrow from one shape to another and it docks to their borders. Move either shape and the connector re-routes itself, instantly, every frame.

Real undo & history

Every edit — move, resize, recolor, delete — is a reversible step. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z walk a true 80-deep snapshot history.

Smart snapping

Drag a shape and it snaps to the edges and centers of its neighbours, with magenta guide lines. Hold Alt to move freely.

Local-first & portable

Your board autosaves to this browser as you work. Export the whole thing to PNG for sharing, or to JSON to back up and re-import anywhere.

Minimap & zoom-to-fit

A live minimap shows the whole board and your viewport; click it to jump. Press 2 to frame everything, or zoom to a selection.

How the engine works

Everything you see is drawn to a single HTML <canvas> on every frame. The camera is just three numbers — an x/y offset and a zoom — and two functions convert between world coordinates (where shapes actually live) and screen pixels. To zoom toward the cursor, Boundless records the world point under your mouse, changes the zoom, then nudges the offset so that same world point lands back under the cursor.

Each object is a plain, serializable record: a rectangle, ellipse, sticky note, text label, freehand stroke, or connector. Because they're just data, the entire board can be snapshotted for undo, saved to localStorage, and round-tripped through JSON. Connectors don't store fixed endpoints — they store the ids of the shapes they link, and recompute their docking points against each shape's current bounds every render. That's why they stay attached.

Why you'd never build this in a page builder

Boundless is a stateful, pointer-driven application: a transform matrix, hit-testing, a marquee, resize handles, an undo stack, snapping, an inline text editor, autosave, and export — all coordinating in real time. It's the opposite of a content page. There are no sections to stack and no posts to publish; there's one live surface that responds to every gesture. That's the whole point.
